description: Create a thread (multiple posts) on X/Twitter, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram, Facebook, or Telegram. Publish to several accounts at once by naming account_ids instead of account_id, and give one of them a thread of its own with account_configurations. X, Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon, and Telegram support native reply threading. Others degrade gracefully to standalone posts. A THREAD IS ATOMIC: if any part fails, every part already published is deleted from the platform and the whole thread's quota is refunded, and the error's `thread_rollback` says what was rolled back. Two codes tell you whether a retry is safe: `upstream_error` means nothing of the thread is on the platform, so repeating the request is safe, while `thread_rollback_incomplete` means the posts named in `thread_rollback.still_live` are still up with their ids and URLs, and repeating the request would publish them twice. On an Instagram account connected by signing in with Instagram, where Chirpie cannot delete a published post, a failed thread always reports its published parts as still live. On X, each post in the thread whose text contains a link is billed at $0.25 on paid plans; on the Free plan such threads are rejected (x_link_posts_require_paid_plan). X accounts connected with your own X API keys are exempt. A thread that would cross the monthly post or scheduled-post quota answers 429 usage_limit_exceeded and publishes nothing; the per-minute burst limit on the API key answers 429 rate_limited. Set draft: true to save the thread without sending it: nothing reaches the platform, nothing counts against the quota, a draft thread may still be a single part long, and the answer carries a `warnings` array. chirpie_update_post on any of its parts promotes it, and the whole thread goes together.

configuration.description: Publishing options for this account's thread only, instead of the shared ones. The whole block is replaced rather than merged.

facebook.description: How a Facebook Page publishes this post.

link.description: A URL to attach to a feed post, shown as a link preview. Feed posts only.

placement.description: Where the post goes on the Page: feed (the default), or story, which takes exactly one image or video, no text and no first comment.

instagram.description: How an Instagram account publishes this post. A story carries no caption (send empty text), no first comment and no collaborators. A reel takes one video, collaborators, user tags, a cover, share_to_feed and trial_reel.

collaborators.description: Up to 3 Instagram usernames to invite as co-authors, without the @. The post appears on a collaborator's profile once they accept the invitation, which happens on Instagram. Feed posts and reels only.

cover.description: The id of an uploaded image to use as a reel's cover. Use this or video_cover_timestamp_ms, never both: Instagram reads the image and ignores the timestamp, so sending both would drop one of the two things you asked for.

placement.description: Where the post goes: feed (the default) takes up to 10 images, story takes exactly one image or video, reel takes exactly one video and no images.

share_to_feed.description: Whether a reel also appears on the profile grid.

trial_reel.description: Publish as a trial reel, shown to people who do not follow the account first. Reels only.

graduation.description: How the reel reaches the account's followers: 'manual' waits for the customer to release it, 'performance' releases it once Instagram decides it is doing well.

user_tags.description: The people to tag. A feed post needs both x and y on every tag, a story may carry both or neither, and a reel takes the username on its own, because Instagram reads coordinates only on images and stories. Tags belong to one image, so a carousel carrying them is refused.

x.description: Distance from the left edge, 0 to 1.

y.description: Distance from the top edge, 0 to 1.

video_cover_timestamp_ms.description: A frame of the reel itself to use as its cover, in milliseconds.

first_comment.description: A first comment for this account's thread only, instead of the shared one. An empty string publishes this account's thread with no first comment.

posts.description: The complete thread for this account, replacing the shared posts rather than merging part by part. Still 2 to 25 parts.

media.description: Uploaded files and public links for this part.

alt.description: A description of the item, for people using a screen reader.

id.description: The id chirpie_upload_media returned. Valid for 7 days.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch.

media_ids.description: Ids from chirpie_upload_media for this part, when no alt text is needed.

media_urls.description: Public image or video URLs for this part.

text.description: Post text for this account's thread.

account_configurations.description: Per-account threads, keyed by account ID. Every key must also be in account_ids. An account with no entry publishes the shared posts.

account_id.description: Account ID to post from (X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Threads, Mastodon, Instagram, Facebook, or Telegram). Some platforms degrade to standalone posts. Use this or account_ids, not both.

account_ids.description: Account IDs to publish the same thread to, 1 to 25 of them, each named once. Naming this instead of account_id answers with a group_id and one result per account, in the order given, each with its own `success`: an account whose platform refused is reported there while the others stay published.

configuration.description: Per-platform publishing options, keyed by platform. Instagram takes a feed post, a story or a reel, and a Facebook Page takes a feed post or a story; leave it out and everything publishes to the feed. Nothing is dropped quietly: a block keyed on a platform that takes no options, on a platform no account in the call uses, or a field the chosen placement does not carry, is refused with 400 configuration_unsupported naming the platform and the field. One block serves every account of that platform; give one account its own with an account_configurations entry. A thread publishes to the feed: an Instagram story or reel, and a Facebook Page story, are each a single post, so a thread asking for one of those placements is refused.

link.description: A URL to attach to a feed post, shown as a link preview. Feed posts only.

placement.description: Where the post goes on the Page: feed (the default), or story, which takes exactly one image or video, no text and no first comment.

x.description: Distance from the left edge, 0 to 1.

y.description: Distance from the top edge, 0 to 1.

video_cover_timestamp_ms.description: A frame of the reel itself to use as its cover, in milliseconds.

draft.description: Save the thread without sending it. Every part is stored with status draft, nothing reaches the platform, and it costs no quota.

first_comment.description: A comment to publish under the thread's LAST post once the thread is out. One comment for the whole thread, not one per part, and reported on that last part's first_comment. Available on X, Threads, Instagram and Facebook only: anywhere else is refused with 400 first_comment_unsupported rather than dropped. It counts as one post against the monthly quota, and it never fails the thread.

idempotency_key.description: A key of your own making that makes retrying this call safe. The same key with the same request replays the first answer for 24 hours instead of sending it again; the same key with a different request is refused with 422 idempotency_key_reused, and a retry that arrives while the first is still running is refused with 409 idempotency_in_progress; a retry after the first has finished collects the replay.

posts.description: Array of posts in the thread. A thread needs at least 2 to publish; a draft may be saved with 1 while it is still being written.

media.description: Uploaded files and public links, each with optional alt text. An entry takes either `id`, from chirpie_upload_media, or `url`, a public link Chirpie fetches. `alt` describes the item for people using a screen reader and is carried to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Instagram and Facebook. Use this or media_urls, not both. Images per post: X 4, Bluesky 4 (977 KB each), LinkedIn 4 (JPEG, PNG, GIF up to 8 MB), Threads 1, Mastodon 4, Instagram 10 (carousel), Facebook 10, Telegram 10. Video: X, Mastodon and Telegram only, one per post and never alongside images. Instagram REQUIRES at least 1 image. Anything a platform cannot take is refused with 400 unsupported_media, never dropped.

alt.description: A description of the item, for people using a screen reader.

id.description: The id chirpie_upload_media returned. Valid for 7 days.

url.description: A public image or video URL for Chirpie to fetch.

media_ids.description: Ids from chirpie_upload_media, for a post that needs no alt text. Same per-platform rules as `media`.

media_urls.description: Public image or video URLs, for a post that needs no alt text. Same per-platform rules as `media`.

text.description: Post text (max 280 chars for standard X, 25,000 for X Premium, 300 for Bluesky, 3,000 for LinkedIn, 500 for Threads, 500 for Mastodon, 2,200 for Instagram, 63,206 for Facebook, 4,096 for Telegram, or 1,024 for Telegram when media_urls is set)

schedule_at.description: ISO 8601 datetime to schedule the thread. Either an absolute instant carrying a timezone, such as '2026-04-01T14:00:00Z' or '2026-04-01T16:00:00+02:00', or a local time with no offset, such as '2026-11-01T09:30:00', which is read in the timezone parameter or the one saved on the account and is refused when there is neither. Scheduled threads publish within ~5 minutes of this time. On a draft it is only the time you have in mind.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone a schedule_at with no offset is read in, such as 'America/New_York'. Daylight saving is worked out for the date named, which is what makes '09:30 on 1 November' come out right. Ignored when schedule_at already carries an offset. Leave it out to use the timezone saved on the account.
